claims.claim: Field intake stays far below gut capacity: across 38 wild species, predators carried two to three times the digestive capacity their mean intake needed (Armstrong & Schindler 2011; abstract only)
claims.location: p. 84 (PDF p. 1), abstract; p. 85 (PDF p. 2), results
claims.quote: capacity to feed at daily rates 2–3 times higher than what they experience on average
claims.conditions: 639 field estimates of p (= C/Cmax, the proportion of maximum consumption solved from observed growth with the Wisconsin bioenergetics model) from 66 populations of 38 fish species (49 lake, 11 marine, 6 stream populations), from 42 articles and 4 theses; median p 0.43 (s.d. 0.16) by population; mean estimation interval 208 d (s.d. 143); 'capacity' is laboratory ad libitum Cmax, not a measured gut; 'predators' are all fish guilds (planktivores and benthivores as well as piscivores)
claims.note: full text read: drop '(abstract only)'. The 2–3× is an inference from bioenergetics fits (capacity/load = 1/p; median 2.3), not a direct measurement of gut volume or evacuation

claims.claim: fish carry 2–3× the digestive capacity they use (Armstrong & Schindler 2011)
claims.quote: median capacity is 2.3 times expected load
claims.conditions: as above: bioenergetics-model p across 66 wild fish populations; fewer than 5 % of populations had p > 0.8
claims.note: the code uses it to justify letting adults refill at up to Q × Cmax; the source supports only that mean field intake is ~0.43 of Cmax, not any particular refill rate

notes: Other values the rewrite could use (pp. 85–86): the median population spends 18–53 % of days feeding below a maintenance ration (< 20 % of Cmax); < 5 % of populations had load:capacity > 0.8; lake, marine and stream populations did not differ (Kruskal–Wallis P = 0.10). A numerical model says excess capacity of this size pays only when daily foraging opportunity is very right-skewed (c.v. ~70–150 %). The paper also argues against reading 'few empty stomachs' (Arrington et al. 2002) as evidence of positive daily energy balance — relevant to the same §3.7.3 paragraph, which cites Arrington's 35 % vs 16 % empty stomachs.
